• • Total training load is the overall demand placed on the body through training.

questions.question: Define flexibility as a health-related fitness component.
questions.solution_html:
• • Flexibility is the ability of a joint to move through its available range of motion.
  • • It supports mobility and efficient performance of functional movements.
questions.final_answer: • Flexibility is the ability of a joint to move through its available range of motion

questions.question: Explain the importance of recovery capacity when applying progressive / overload.
questions.solution_html:
• • Recovery capacity is the body's ability to repair itself and adapt after exercise.
  • • Adequate recovery supports muscle repair and replenishment of energy stores.
  • • Training load should be increased according to individual fitness and recovery ability.
  • • Insufficient recovery may cause excessive fatigue, reduced performance, and injury.
  • • Adequate sleep, nutrition, hydration, and rest days support training adaptations.
questions.final_answer: • Adequate sleep, nutrition, hydration, and rest days support training adaptations
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: A trainee sustains an acute injury during exercise. Explain how the gym / instructor should respond while ensuring the safety of the casualty and others present.
questions.solution_html:
• A trainee sustains an acute injury during exercise. Explain the response required to
  • ensure the safety of the casualty and others.
  • • Stop the exercise immediately and ensure the surrounding area is safe.
  • • Assess the casualty's responsiveness, breathing, and severity of injury.
  • • Call emergency services for serious injuries and provide first aid within the limits of
  • one's training.
  • • Avoid unnecessary movement, especially if a spinal injury is suspected.
  • • Reassure and monitor the casualty while keeping other participants away from the
  • injured area.
questions.final_answer: injured area
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain iodine, its functions, sources, and deficiency disorders.
questions.solution_html:
• • Iodine is an essential mineral required for the production of thyroid hormones.
  • • Thyroid hormones regulate metabolism, growth, and brain development.
  • • Sources include iodized salt, seafood, fish, dairy products, and eggs.
  • • Iodine deficiency may cause goitre and hypothyroidism.
  • • Severe deficiency during pregnancy and early childhood may impair brain development
  • and physical growth.
questions.final_answer: and physical growth
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain why the same repetition total may be distributed across sets in / different ways and how this can affect training demand.
questions.solution_html:
• ways, and how does this affect training demand?
  • • The same total repetitions can be divided differently, such as 30 repetitions performed
  • as 3 × 10 or 5 × 6.
  • • Fewer repetitions per set may help maintain proper technique and control fatigue within
  • each set.
  • • More repetitions per set may increase local muscular fatigue.
  • • Shorter rest intervals may increase fatigue, while longer rest intervals may improve
  • performance in subsequent sets.
  • • Training demand depends on resistance, number of sets and repetitions, rest intervals
  • and individual goals.
questions.final_answer: and individual goals
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: What is progression? Explain how it should be applied when planning / an exercise programme.
questions.solution_html:
• • Progression is the gradual increase in training demand as the body adapts to exercise.
  • • Assess the individual's health, fitness level, experience, and exercise technique.
  • • Gradually increase resistance, repetitions, sets, duration, frequency, or exercise
  • difficulty.
  • • Individualize the programme according to the person's goals, ability, and response to
  • training.
  • • Monitor progress and provide adequate recovery to improve fitness and minimize
  • injury risk.
questions.final_answer: injury risk
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the functions of fats in the human body and differentiate / between saturated and unsaturated fats.
questions.solution_html:
• • Fats provide approximately 9 kcal of energy per gram and serve as an energy reserve.
  • • They insulate the body, protect internal organs, and support the absorption of vitamins
  • A, D, E, and K.
  • • Saturated fats: Commonly found in butter, fatty meat, and coconut oil.
  • • Unsaturated fats: Found in nuts, seeds, vegetable oils, and fatty fish.
  • • Replacing saturated fats with unsaturated fats can help support cardiovascular health.
questions.final_answer: • Replacing saturated fats with unsaturated fats can help support cardiovascular health
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
